text:
**Top pick: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-150)**

It's the best all-rounder for pool and beach. It has an IP68 rating (dust-tight, survives submersion), 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and strong, clear sound. It can also charge your phone. What Hi-Fi lists it at $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon. [What Hi-Fi's review and buy links](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) | [Best Products' review](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Other picks by need**

- **Pool party or big groups: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS' best waterproof speaker. It floats, handles long immersion, gets loud, and lasts over 40 hours. It's big and pricey, and its sound is directional, so it's best aimed at your group. [RTINGS review](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Even sound all around: Ultimate Ears Epicboom.** Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range. It's IP67, floats, and has 360-degree sound, but only 15 hours of battery. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 (about $65-80).** It's IP67, floats, has 360-degree sound, and gets 14 hours. It's small, so it's not very loud. [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **Easy to carry: JBL Grip (about $100).** Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, can-sized, under a pound, and gets 12 hours. The mesh body can get dusty. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Cheapest: JBL Go 5 (about $40).** It's IP67 with 8 hours of battery, and very small. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)
- **Loud, floating party speaker: Soundcore Boom 2 Plus.** It's 100 W, rated IPX7, floats, and gets 20 hours at half volume. It's heavy at 3.8 kg and has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach. It lists at $249.99, or $200 with code AFSC20 (which Dealectric tested on 2026-10-22). That link is an affiliate link. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus)

**Tips**

- Look for IP67 or higher. For the beach, a dust rating (the first number, 5 or 6) matters too.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use, keep the charging port closed, and dry it fully before charging. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/))
- Prices change, so check the current price at checkout.

For one speaker that does both pool and beach, I'd get the Charge 6. If you mostly host pool parties, get the Boombox 4 or Epicboom.
